newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Central RR braces for millennium bug.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Central RR braces for millennium bug.

text.p: Illinois Central Railroad Corp, a unit of Illinois Central Corp, said Thursday it expects that it would cost $2 million to modify its existing computer software programs for the year 2000.

In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the Chicago-based railroad said it is now evaluating the costs of making such modifications to handle potential computer bugs in the millennium.
Problems are expected to arise from computers that record only the last two digits of a year -- such systems might treat 2000 as 1900, causing serious miscalculations.
"Current estimates are approximately $2 million," the company said, adding that it may also decide to completely replace its "non-2000" compliant programs.
"A final determination is expected in the fourth quarter of 1997," the railroad said.
The company's preparations for the year 2000 come as many corporations and even federal regulators are bracing themselves for potential software bugs.
